title: How testimony reaches the record
notes: Added: the witness-chain domain node becomes an explainer. CLAUDE.md section 2a requires every notability node to say how its claim reached us; this topic explains circular reporting, single interviewers and the difference between agreement in substance and verbatim agreement.

lead.text: Testimony reaches this board by routes that shape what it is worth: the author of the Dulce literature's central insider said in a 2015 email that he had invented him and had mailed a hundred packets of material to other writers, and the Disclosure Project's sixty-eight testimonies were all taken by one interviewer.

summary.text: A witness admitted for notability is anchored on the dated artefact of the claim, not on a record of the thing claimed, so each such node has to say how the claim reached us: who found the witness and how, what the witness said before contact with an interested party, and whether the accounts agree in detail or only in substance.

The board carries two documented cases of many voices with one origin, one deliberate and one not: Tal Levesque's confessed seeding of the Dulce story, and the Disclosure Project cohort, collected and cross-referenced by its own compiler.

Between those poles sit interviewer-led registers, such as Robert Hastings's nuclear-site witnesses, and the control cases in which a witness came forward on his own, such as the Minot B-52 co-pilot who approached a research body in 2000.

Formal channels leave a different kind of trace: sworn hearing testimony, the Defense Department Inspector General's evaluation opened on personnel complaints, and the Intelligence Community Inspector General's urgent-concern form. A document entered into a hearing record by a member is not a witness appearance.

record.text: The photograph circulated for years as Thomas Castello's leaked evidence of bodies in a chamber at Dulce is a frame from the 2000 film The 6th Day, as John Greenewald showed in 2016; anyone can check it against the film.

The Disclosure Project Briefing Document of April 2001 prints sixty-eight dated testimony headings; every transcript carries an initials key naming Greer as interviewer, his comments are printed inside the witness text, and his bracketed notes cross-reference his own witnesses to each other.

The printed record of the 9 September 2025 House hearing shows Rep. Burlison entering testimonies he said Steven Greer had given him, including Michael Herrera's; Herrera is on no committee witness list and his name appears once across three hearing records, in that colloquy.

AARO's historical report of February 2024 summarises, without names, an interviewee's claim of seeing Special Forces load containers onto a craft in 2009, and states that interviewees were assigned random numbers with the key held by AARO; about 30 people had been interviewed by 17 September 2023.

The documentary half of an interviewer's output can be checked separately from the interviews: the board opened the 341st Strategic Missile Wing histories and the 24th NORAD Region log that Hastings relies on and found them saying what he says, while the Warren Blue Book telephone log was read only through a mirror of Hastings's own material.

Some accounts are fixed in time before any interviewer arrived: the 1968 Minot debriefing record names Capt. Bradford Runyon as co-pilot, and Robert Jacobs published his own account in the MUFON UFO Journal in January 1989.

The House Oversight Committee heard sworn testimony from David Grusch, David Fravor and Ryan Graves on 26 July 2023; the Defense Department Inspector General's evaluation DODIG-2023-109 was opened after complaints from personnel; and the Intelligence Community Inspector General publishes the form for disclosing an urgent concern.

claimed.text: Levesque, who wrote as Jason Bishop III, told Adam Gorightly by email in November 2015 that Castello was a creation, a myth, built from the account of a woman he names as Ann West, corrected and mixed with his own research into the two original Dulce Base articles. He had maintained for years in the same correspondence that Castello was real. Gorightly's 2021 book printed the email.

In the same message Levesque described how the appearance of independent corroboration was made: he sent a hundred large envelope packets of material on underground bases, genetic research and hidden science to authors and lecturers, who mixed it into their talks, articles and books.

The Dulce story's specific numbers all come from one later lecture, Phil Schneider's at Post Falls, Idaho on 8 May 1995. On the board's reading, the woman Levesque names as his raw material may also be the route by which John Lear came to the story in 1988, which would put two entry points through one person.
Greer claimed at the 2001 press conference some 400 witnesses willing to testify to Congress; the cohort the board can see is the sixty-eight printed testimonies, of which it has checked eight.

In the Malmstrom register, Walter Figel's account exists as Hastings's recordings of three telephone calls, Frederick Meiwald's as a letter to the claimant and Hastings's recordings, Robert Jamison's as the source of a date Hastings uses, and Robert Kaminski's as a 1997 letter to a researcher; Hastings's method of finding witnesses is stated nowhere the board has opened.

At Ellsworth, Mario Woods had told his account under his own name since 1996, naming Michael Johnson on air and asking audiences to find him. Johnson was then located by the publishing party from a viewer's Facebook tip; nothing he said about the event before that contact exists; and on the recorded call he first said no when asked what they encountered, assenting only after Woods twice asked whether it was a UFO.

The two Ellsworth accounts agree on substance and diverge on posture and agency, Johnson passive and Woods active; on the board's reading that pattern reads very differently from verbatim agreement and is the strongest point in the second account's favour.

The self-initiated cases run the other way: Runyon contacted the Center for UFO Studies himself in 2000; Robert Salas, a claimant who never said he saw anything himself, approached the Great Falls Tribune himself in 1996; the Warren 1965 reports reached the public because Project Blue Book's own consultant printed its log; and Jacobs published under his own name years before any interviewer sought him out.

Fravor gave the chain for the Nimitz case under oath: the incident lay dormant until Jay Stratton contacted him in 2009 to investigate for a Pentagon programme; years later Alex Dietrich contacted him to ask whether he had been approached; then Lue Elizondo contacted him.
Herrera's own account is on a dated podcast recording of July 2023. The board infers, with no record making the link, that the anonymous interviewee on page 29 of AARO's report is Herrera.

contested.text: On the board's reading, the Levesque confession means that the many later Dulce sources agree because one person supplied them by one method, which is the board's own rule made real: two sources agreeing is not corroboration when they share a method.

Nothing independent supports the Castello figure: Greenewald found no evidence the man existed, and the claim attaches no jurisdiction, employer or dates to the name, so no records search can even be framed. Norio Hayakawa, who has worked the Dulce question since 1988, says the base does not seem to exist.

The Disclosure Project document is Tier 1 for the fact that a named person gave testimony on a stated date and Tier 2 at best for its content, because it was compiled by an interested party who also conducted the interviews; the corroboration its notes assert is the compiler's own.

Interview-led registers carry the circularity risk in plain form: four Malmstrom witnesses sharing a single interviewer are one method applied four times, the interviewer's own separation of two events rests on a witness he interviewed, and his count of witnesses varies between his own pages.

The Ellsworth episode's own later retelling has Johnson recognising the event with nothing supplied, which its recording of the call does not show; and the two accounts cannot be treated as independent, because Woods's version named Johnson for thirty years before he was found.
Promotional language is not a record: the claim that Herrera is testifying to Congress is unsupported, and he has never been a hearing witness.

Independence can also be shown: Philip Klass and Kevin Randle reached the same discrepancies in Clifford Stone's account by different methods, one from a records request to the National Personnel Records Center and one from thirty years of acquaintance, so the shared-method caution does not apply to that pair.

The Malmstrom corroboration is itself disputed: James Carlson says Figel told him he saw no UFO and treated the radio report as a joke, Tim Hebert says Figel's two Hastings interviews contradict each other and that Figel declined to sign an affidavit, and Meiwald's 1996 letter is characterised in two incompatible ways, one reading it as recording a different recollection from the claimant's.

questions: For each witness admitted on notability, who found them, by what route, and what had they said in public before that contact?
Were any witnesses shown or told another witness's account before giving their own, and where that happened, what did they say before it?
Which of the many sources that repeat the Dulce story can be traced to Levesque's hundred packets, and which, if any, arose independently?
How did Hastings locate the veterans he interviewed, and did any of them approach him first?
For the fifty-seven unchecked Disclosure Project testimonies, is there any earlier dated statement by the witness, made before Greer interviewed them?
Where two accounts agree, is the agreement in substance with divergent detail, or verbatim, and does any shared intermediary explain it?
